material.title: lemo-opuscar · 66 种代码影片风格
material.summary: 66 种影片风格，每种配一支完全由代码逐帧渲染的示范短片（Canvas / WebGL 画面、免费采样配乐、本地 TTS 旁白），附导演、技术指南与“改成我的风格”流程。
material.carrierNote: 风格示范片用浏览器页面按时间逐帧渲染后合成视频，最终形态为视频，归入本库。
workflow: 确定主题并选风格，一次询问事实、用户素材、语言与是否先看分镜，再补齐其余简报。
打开示范制作说明前，按 DIRECTOR.md 写 TREATMENT.md 的三套候选结构、取舍、镜头、节拍与声音安排。
读取所选 STYLE.md 的画面、色彩、字体、动作、镜头与声音不变量，用实际绘图代码做风格帧。
从 demo 学笔刷、绑定、着色器与混音技术，把故事、道具、镜头和时间轴写成用户主题。
按 TECHNIQUE.md 制作旁白与语音识别、采样配乐、逐帧画面、拟音、混音和视频合成，风格规定的帧率优先。
按 DIRECTOR.md 自检声音、节奏、运镜、表演与交付文件，用户要求分镜时先等待分镜审阅。
MY-STYLES.md 的五步是逐题规划、确认摘要、用代码比较风格帧、制作15–30秒示范片、用户确认后保存到个人风格目录。
useCases: 按指定风格制作主题短片与科普、旅行、品牌、纪实影片
借用笔刷、布局、点云、微缩模型、声音和逐帧渲染技术
把现有风格改成品牌或频道自己的风格，或从空白开始保存个人风格
avoid: 上游声明为 Claude Opus 5.5 调校，其他模型可能难以复现。
单支影片约需30–60分钟 Agent 时间与相应 token。
运行环境需要 Node 20+、ffmpeg 7+、Python 3.11+（或 uv）。

license.name: MIT · CC BY 4.0
license.notes: README 的 Licence 节：代码和文档（含风格文本）MIT；styles、画廊与 Releases 中的示范影片及静帧 CC BY 4.0，署名 LemoLab 并链接仓库，改编注明改动；用户新做影片归用户。第三方资源保留原许可。game-show 的 macOS say 喊声、paper-lantern 的 Edge TTS 旁白、news-package 的豆包 TTS 旁白被明确排除在 CC BY 4.0 外。

material.install:
claude plugin marketplace add lemomo-ai/lemo-opuscar
claude plugin install lemo-opuscar@lemolab

或：
git clone https://github.com/lemomo-ai/lemo-opuscar.git
cd lemo-opuscar
claude

relatedEntries.note: 从澳大利亚红色腹地沿降雨梯度横移到绿色海岸，植物逐笔画入，纸雾洗去风景后展开大陆地图，回溯五千万年的干湿变化。
五条规则把音乐会海报排进网格，唯一的红圆脱离格点，带动版面重排；海报旋转后揭示为正在播放的乐谱，再拉远成一墙变体。
康涅狄格州阿什福德的一片森林，从夏季航拍转为春季激光点云；切割面剥去树冠，地面凝成受光表面，显出 22 段、合计 3.4 公里的旧农田石墙。
一个虚构河湾在连续高视角镜头中经历四季：广场主树每次下蹲回弹，换季波从树扩散，地面、树冠、屋顶与水面依次改色，冬日窗灯逐盏亮起。

documents.research:
# lemo-opuscar

Lemomo（[@lemomo-ai](https://github.com/lemomo-ai)）的代码影片风格库，包含66种风格、每种的示范短片、导演和技术指南，以及串起98部奥斯卡最佳影片的长片 OPUSCAR 98。本库原文快照固定在 [`f17136060781a0068a7951245a3aa7835a7230de`](https://github.com/lemomo-ai/lemo-opuscar/tree/f17136060781a0068a7951245a3aa7835a7230de)；代码与文档为 MIT，示范成片和静帧为 CC BY 4.0，第三方资源与配音例外见[素材条目的许可](../../materials.html#material/lemo-opuscar)。

## 组成

| 文件 | 提供的内容 |
| --- | --- |
| DIRECTOR.md | 故事、声音、节奏、运镜、表演和交付自检的导演方法。 |
| TECHNIQUE.md | 环境、逐帧页面、旁白、配乐、混音与合成。 |
| styles/<slug>/STYLE.md | 风格的外观、配色、字体、动作、镜头语法、声音与原生招式。 |
| styles/<slug>/DEMO.md | 对应示范片的故事、镜头、配乐结构、道具、参数与制作说明。 |
| MY-STYLES.md | 改造库内风格或从空白制作并保存个人风格的五步流程。 |
| core/ | 渲染、TTS、语音识别、采样乐器、拟音、混音，以及基础随机、缓动与 Three.js 后期工具。 |

## 用法

在终端安装插件后，可以从任意文件夹开始：

```sh
claude plugin marketplace add lemomo-ai/lemo-opuscar
claude plugin install lemo-opuscar@lemolab
```

也可克隆仓库，在库内运行 Claude：

```sh
git clone https://github.com/lemomo-ai/lemo-opuscar.git
cd lemo-opuscar
claude
```

直接说想要的主题、时长和风格。上游 README 的两个示例：

> Make a 45-second film in the **watercolor** style about the coffee farm my family runs. Warm female narrator.

> Make a 40-second **LiDAR Survey** film about the old quarry in the hills behind our town, from public laser-scan data.

Agent 先一次询问三件事：主题中需要用户决定的事实；用户自己的声音、音乐或其他素材；是否先审阅分镜。语言由请求确定，默认与用户使用的语言相同。安装插件后空调用 `/lemo-opuscar:lemo-opuscar` 可先选语言，再选制作影片、改风格或使用已保存风格。

---
name: lemo-opuscar
description: Direct and produce a short film made entirely in code, in one of the styles of the Lemo-Opuscar library (e.g. Impasto Oil Painting 油画厚涂, Watercolor Brush 水彩笔刷, Ukiyo-e 浮世绘, Satellite Briefing 卫星简报, Exploded Teardown 产品拆解). Use when the user asks for a video, film, short, promo, explainer or animation (视频、短片、动画、宣传片) in a named style, including explainers built from real material such as satellite imagery, laser scans, CAD files or archive scans (数据解说、科普、产品拆解), and new films cut from real archive footage and documents (剪辑与纪实, e.g. 用档案影像剪一支新闻片); when they want a film about their own topic and haven't chosen a style (help them choose); when they want to change a style into their own, make their own style from a blank page, or use a style they saved (改风格、从空白开始、我的风格); when they start the skill without saying what they want; or when they ask which film styles there are. Not for plain editing, trimming or converting the user's existing video files.
---

# Lemo-Opuscar

The styles, guides and tools live in the Lemo-Opuscar library (github.com/lemomo-ai/lemo-opuscar). This skill fetches it and hands you over to it.

1. **Get the library.** Run `sh "<skill base directory>/scripts/setup.sh"`. It clones or updates the library (default `~/lemo-opuscar`; a clone the user is standing in is used as it is) and prints `LIB=<path>` on its last line.
2. **Install the core tools early.** Start `sh "<skill base directory>/scripts/setup.sh" deps` right away, in the background if you can: it takes a few minutes the first time. Add `deps voice` or `deps music` later, only if the film needs them (`$LIB/TECHNIQUE.md` §1). Report missing system tools (Node, ffmpeg, Python) in your one round of questions; don't install system software yourself. Packages a style needs (its `STYLE.md` lists them) you install yourself, into the project folder.
3. **Follow the library.** Read `$LIB/AGENTS.md` and do what it says, starting with **Start** (the user's own styles in `~/lemo-my-styles/`; when they started the skill without writing anything, the language question first, then the ways in): finding the style or making their own, the one round of questions, the treatment, production and delivery.

What changes in skill mode:

| | |
|---|---|
| Project folder | `<name>/` in the folder the user started from (lowercase letters, digits, hyphens; avoid `#` and `?` in the path). Wherever the guides say `films/<name>/`, read this folder |
| Running tools | from `$LIB`, with the project's absolute path: `cd "$LIB" && node core/render/still.mjs "<project>" 1.5 3` |
| Library files in pages | absolute URLs: `/core/lib.js`, `/node_modules/three/…` (the project is served at `/@film/`) |
| Library files in scripts and `build.sh` | `$LIB/…`, with `LIB=<path>` at the top of `build.sh`; never `../..` |
| Demo source | not downloaded. `sh "<skill base directory>/scripts/setup.sh" demo <slug>`, only after your `TREATMENT.md` is written, to read its techniques; it is not meant to be rendered. An Edit & Documentary style is the exception: fetch it before the treatment to use the material tools its `STYLE.md` names in `demo/tools/` (`$LIB/AGENTS.md`, "Treatment first") |

Deliver what `$LIB/DIRECTOR.md` §11 lists, in the project folder, and tell the user where it is.

# Lemo-Opuscar: instructions for agents

This repository is a library of film styles. Each style has a `styles/<slug>/STYLE.md` (what the style is) and one demo film made entirely in code (`DEMO.md` and `demo/`). People pick a style and ask for a film about **their own** topic. Your job is to direct and produce that film.

| The request | Go to |
|---|---|
| Any request: first see the user's own styles; no request yet: offer the ways in | **Start** below |
| A film about the user's topic (the normal case) | **Style and story**, **Workflow** below |
| "Which styles are there?" / no style chosen | **Finding the style** below |
| Directing: story, sound, rhythm, camera, checks, delivery | [`DIRECTOR.md`](DIRECTOR.md) |
| Building: install, pages, voice, music, mix | [`TECHNIQUE.md`](TECHNIQUE.md) |
| Tool commands and flags | [`core/README.md`](core/README.md) |
| The user wants to change a style and keep it as their own, or make their own style from a blank page, or names a style in `~/lemo-my-styles/` | [`MY-STYLES.md`](MY-STYLES.md) |
| Adding a style to the library (owner only) | [`MAINTAINING.md`](MAINTAINING.md) |

**Films outside `styles/` are the user's: no LemoLab credit, no watermark.**

## Start

- **Their own styles first.** If `~/lemo-my-styles/README.md` exists, read it: it lists every style the user has saved, wherever it's kept, and their own styles ([`MY-STYLES.md`](MY-STYLES.md)) count like library styles. When they name a style, look there first, then in the library.
- **Their language.** Talk to them in the language they write in. When they started the skill without writing anything, your first question is always the language, even when their settings, memory or earlier messages suggest one: the `AskUserQuestion` tool, a question of its own headed "Language 语言" with two options, 中文 and English (the tool adds Other, where they type any other language). Use it from then on, and as the film's default language.
- **No request yet** (they only started the skill, or said hello): offer the ways in with one question, using the `AskUserQuestion` tool, in their language, with the first as the recommended one:
  1. a film in a library style (**Finding the style**);
  2. change a library style and keep it as their own ([`MY-STYLES.md`](MY-STYLES.md));
  3. make their own style from a blank page ([`MY-STYLES.md`](MY-STYLES.md));
  4. a film in one of their own styles, only when they have some (name them).

  When their request already says which, skip the question.

## Style and story

- **`STYLE.md` is fixed**: the style's invariants (look, colour, type, motion, camera grammar, sound palette, native moves, pitfalls). Keep all of it.
- **Everything else is yours to direct** from the user's topic: story, structure, characters, settings, shots, timings, references, how data is charted. Never bend the topic toward the demo.
- **Treatment first, demo later.** Write your own `TREATMENT.md`, with three candidate structures and your choice (DIRECTOR.md §4), before you open `DEMO.md` or the demo code. Then use the demo only to learn techniques (a brush engine, a rig, a shader, a mix), never its story, arc, shots, props or timeline. One exception: a style cut from real material (Edit & Documentary) needs its material before the treatment, so the tools its `STYLE.md` names in `demo/tools/` for finding and logging material (`footage.py` and the like) may be used first, copied into the project folder and run there; still read `DEMO.md` and the rest of the demo only after the treatment is written.
- **Scene styles** (a set-up guide, a spec walkthrough, a museum plate, a trail guide) list use cases in their `STYLE.md`. Read them as grammar for the order in which information arrives and how long each part needs on screen, then build the user's content in your own structure. Swapping text into a demo's `content.json` is only a technical check, never the way to deliver.
- Never build inside `styles/`: copy what you need into the film's project folder.

## Finding the style

Users name a style by its gallery name in English or Chinese ("Impasto Oil Painting", "油画厚涂") or by its folder (`impasto`). Look it up in [`styles/README.md`](styles/README.md). If nothing matches clearly, show the closest two or three and ask.

If the user hasn't picked a style:
- Suggest two or three that fit their topic.
- If they have their own styles, list those first, under "My styles" (in their language).
- Show them the full list below in the chat, in the user's language only: English names (and English category names) for someone writing in English, Chinese names for someone writing in Chinese. Don't drop, merge or rename anything.
- Link the gallery, where every style has its demo film: https://lemomo-ai.github.io/lemo-opuscar/
- Then ask them to type the name. The list goes in your own message (a command's output isn't shown to them), and the question is plain text, not `AskUserQuestion`: its few options would hide the rest of the list.

<!-- style-list:start -->
All 66 styles · 全部风格:

- **剪辑与纪实 Edit & Documentary** (8): 字幕新闻 Caption News, 1920s 新闻影片 1920s Newsreel, 实时倒计时分屏 Live Countdown Split-screen, 延时交响 Time-lapse Symphony, 视觉调查 Visual Investigation, 构成主义蒙太奇 Constructivist Montage, 体育战术板 Sports Telestrator, 电视新闻包装 Broadcast News Package
- **实证影像 Evidence Films** (8): 卫星简报 Satellite Briefing, 工程简报板 Engineering Briefing Board, 点云测绘 LiDAR Survey, 白模投影 Projection on White Model, 数据实物化 Data Physicalization, 产品拆解 Exploded Teardown, 显微叙事 Microscope Story, 档案灯台 Archive Light Table
- **手绘与绘画 Hand-drawn & Painting** (8): 蜡笔儿童绘本 Crayon Picture Book, 水彩笔刷 Watercolor Brush, 中国水墨 Chinese Ink Wash, 油画厚涂 Impasto Oil Painting, 一笔画 One-line Drawing, 白板讲解 Whiteboard Explainer, 钢笔淡彩 Urban Sketch · Pen & Wash, 黑板粉笔 Chalkboard
- **东方传统 East Asian Traditions** (4): 皮影戏 Shadow Puppetry, 浮世绘 Ukiyo-e, 红色窗花剪纸 Red Paper-cut, 纸雕灯影 Paper-cut Lightbox
- **印刷与版画 Print & Printmaking** (6): Risograph 孔版印刷 Risograph Print, 复古半调案卷 Halftone Dossier, 木刻版画 Woodcut Print, 铜版画 Copperplate Engraving, 丝印旅行海报 Silkscreen Travel Poster, 印刷长镜头 Printed Long Take
- **图形与排版 Graphic & Type** (7): 瑞士动态排版 Swiss Motion Graphics, 60s 间谍片头 60s Spy Title Sequence, 装饰艺术 Art Deco, 蓝图 / 工程制图 Blueprint, 彩色玻璃窗 Stained Glass, 象形运动图形 Pictogram Motion, ASCII / CRT 终端 ASCII / CRT Terminal
- **信息与发布 Information & Keynote** (8): 数据叙事 Data Storytelling, 等距信息图 Isometric Infographic, 暗色科技发布 Dark Tech Keynote, 活体实机录屏 Living Screencast, 科幻全息界面 Sci-fi Hologram HUD, 地铁线路图 Transit Map, 等距绘本 Isometric Picture Book, 电路板 Circuit Board
- **卡通与动画 Cartoon & Anime** (4): 1930s 橡皮管卡通 1930s Rubber Hose Cartoon, 80 年代赛璐璐动画 80s Cel Anime, 科幻情景喜剧卡通 Sci-Fi Sitcom Toon, 50s 扁平卡通 Mid-century Cartoon
- **游戏 Games** (4): 16-bit 像素 RPG 16-bit Pixel RPG, HD-2D, 微游戏快闪 Microgame Frenzy, 综艺节奏扁平 Game Show Flat
- **电影与时代 Cinema & Eras** (2): 1920s 默片 1920s Silent Film, 后室 / 新怪谈 Liminal Found Footage
- **材质与 3D Materials & 3D** (7): 积木玩具 Brick Toy, 纸片立体书 Paper Pop-up Book, 移轴微缩 Tilt-Shift Miniature, 低多边形等距 Low-poly Isometric Island, 玻璃质感产品 Glass Product Render, 孟菲斯微缩景观 Memphis Diorama, 桌面穿梭 Desktop Flythrough
<!-- style-list:end -->

## Workflow

1. **Brief.** Make sure the style and the topic are clear, then ask the user once, in a single message (DIRECTOR.md §1):
   - anything about the topic you can't decide yourself (facts; names, logos or products that must appear);
   - whether they have material of their own: a voice recording or a preferred voice, music, photos, logos, fonts, and for a style built from real material, their own data or scans;
   - the film's language, if it isn't obvious (default: the language they write in or chose, for voice and subtitles);
   - whether they want to review a storyboard first (default: no);
   - anything missing on their machine: first run `sh plugin/skills/lemo-opuscar/scripts/setup.sh deps` from the library root (core only) and include what it reports. Add the voice and music tiers later, only if the film needs them (TECHNIQUE.md §1).

   Skip what their request already answers. Wait for the reply, fill every other gap with a sensible default, sum up the brief in a few lines and start. Don't come back with more questions.
2. **Treatment.** Write `TREATMENT.md` in the project folder (DIRECTOR.md §4), before you open the demo (an Edit & Documentary style gathers its material first: **Treatment first** above).
3. **Look.** Render style frames or a model sheet with the real drawing code and check them against `STYLE.md` (DIRECTOR.md §5).
4. **Storyboard, only if the user asked for it** (DIRECTOR.md §5). **Stop and wait for approval.** Otherwise don't stop.
5. **Produce.** Voice → check → score (can run in parallel) → animation → mix → render (TECHNIQUE.md).
6. **Self-check and deliver** (DIRECTOR.md §11).

Report progress in the user's language. If a step fails, read the error, fix the cause and retry; go back to the user only for a decision or something only they can provide.

## Where things go

- The film's project folder is `films/<name>/` in a clone (ignored by git), or `<name>/` in the user's folder in skill mode (see the skill's `SKILL.md`). Wherever a guide says `films/<name>/`, read "the project folder". Work only there, unless the user asks you to work in their own project.
- Run `node core/…` and `sh tools/…` from the library root (`$LIB` in skill mode).
- `core/` has ready-made tools (rendering, TTS, speech check, sampler, sfx, mux). Use them or your own stack, but don't edit `core/` or `styles/` for a user's film.
- Never kill processes you didn't start. Don't leave background processes running.

# Directing a Lemo-Opuscar film

The directing method behind every film in this library. Pair it with one `styles/<slug>/STYLE.md` (the style) and [`TECHNIQUE.md`](TECHNIQUE.md) (how to build).

You are the director, not a tech demo. A film is judged in this order: **sound, rhythm, camera, directing** (performance, staging, emotional arc). Good-looking frames are only the starting point.

---

## 1. Take the brief

The user gives a style and a topic, sometimes more (length, language, voice, must-have shots, brand rules). Everything else is your decision. Ask once, in a single message (AGENTS.md, Workflow), then no more questions. Defaults:

- Length **30–60 s**; shorter and tight beats padded. Beyond two or three minutes multiplies time and token cost: tell the user.
- 1920×1080 at 24 fps by default; an output frame rate set in the style's `STYLE.md` (30 or 60 fps, for example) wins, and is what you pass to `--fps` and `mux.sh`; other sizes (vertical 1080×1920, for example) with `--size WxH` on the render tools.
- Voice and subtitles in the language the user writes in. Subtitles burned in and exported as `.srt`.
- Loudness −14 LUFS.

Say it in the questions when it matters: a good Chinese voice uses Microsoft's online service (edge-tts) and needs a connection; offline, Kokoro reads Chinese but sounds plain (TECHNIQUE.md §4).

Requests that only change the plan:

- **No voice, or no subtitles.** Drop those steps and say so in the treatment.
- **Their own voice recording.** Use it as it is; transcribe it with faster-whisper for word timings.
- **Their own material**: logos, photos, footage, and for styles built from real material (the Evidence Films) their own data, scans, imagery or CAD. Ask whether they have any; what they give comes first, and the sources in the `STYLE.md` are the fallback. Before you download from those sources, tell the user what you will fetch, from where and under which licence. Rights: section 12.

## 2. Find a benchmark first

Before writing anything, pick one or two reference works (films, title sequences, games, ads) that set the bar for this style **and this topic**. They are your choice, made for the user's film; don't borrow the demo's. Write down:

- **What to learn**: composition, pacing, camera grammar, colour logic, score structure.
- **What not to take**: characters, designs, melodies, specific shots, logos, fonts.

The benchmark lifts quality more than any rule below.

## 3. Shape the story

- **One subject, one goal, one turn.** A character (or a single object, product or idea) wants something, something changes, it ends differently from how it began.
- **Hook in the first 3 seconds.** No slow logo reveal before anything happens.
- **An ending that echoes.** Bookend the opening, reveal the scale, or let the character do the thing right the second time.
- **One native move**: a moment only this medium can do (a fold that becomes a transition, ink that blooms into the next scene, a type grid that snaps into the logo). Put it at the emotional peak. `STYLE.md` lists the medium's native moves; pick or invent the one your story needs.
- **Cut the extras.** One gag the audience reads at thumbnail size beats three they can't. If a beat needs explaining, remove it.

## 4. Write the treatment

Write `TREATMENT.md` before drawing anything, and before you open the style's `DEMO.md` or demo code (an Edit & Documentary style gathers its material first: AGENTS.md, "Treatment first"):

1. **Three candidate structures**, a few lines each (for example: a single journey, a before/after, a countdown, a list that turns), then the one you chose and why. Choose the opening image, the ending and the shape of the score from the topic too; the first idea that comes to mind for a style is usually its cliché.
2. **Logline and arc**: one sentence, then setup → turn → ending.
3. **Benchmark**: learn / don't learn (section 2).
4. **Shot list**: for every shot, the framing (wide / full / medium / close / insert), angle, camera move (push, pull, pan, track, crane, zoom), duration, and **why** it is shot that way.
5. **Beat sheet**, second by second.
6. **Cue map**: tempo, bar grid, instrumentation per section, and on which beat every cut, key action and subtitle lands.
7. **Sound design table**: for each section, the ambience bed, the main foley and the music state.
8. **Subtitle and title design**: the type is part of the style.

## 5. Prove the look

- **With characters**: draw a model sheet (turnaround, 3–4 expressions, 2–3 key poses, palette) plus two style frames.
- **Without characters**: three style frames from the film, one of them the signature shot.

Render them with the real drawing code, not a mock-up, and check them yourself against the `STYLE.md` before going on.

### The storyboard (only if the user asked for one)

Render 6–9 key shots with the real drawing code, tiled into one sheet (`core/render/sheet.py`) with shot number, framing, duration and line under each. Send it with the logline and what you are least sure about, and **wait for approval**. If the user didn't ask for one, don't stop.

## 6. Sound is half the film

- **Every visible action has a sound**: landings, page turns, cuts, drips, clicks, cloth. Match the material (paper, wood, metal, ink and glass all sound different).
- **Three layers**: ambience (room, wind, rain, city), foley (tied to actions) and music. Duck the music under dialogue and key foley.
- **At least two real silences**, or near-silences, before the turn or the emotional peak. The first sound after the silence should be one of the most important sounds in the film.
- **Use sound as a transition** at least twice: bring the next scene's sound in early (J-cut) or let the last scene's sound run over the cut (L-cut).
- **Avoid generic "piano and strings".** Score in the instruments of the style's sound palette.

## 7. Rhythm: the music grid comes first

- Write the cue map before animating. The picture locks to the grid, and a script checks every cue (TECHNIQUE.md §3).
- **Vary the pace**: alternate fast and slow, include one clear acceleration or deceleration, and give the audience one breath (a long take or a held pause). A film at one even speed has failed.
- One action, one sound, one cut, but don't cut on every beat. Leave time to see.
- **Pace for the viewer, not the clock**:
  - Hold every subtitle at least 1.8 s, and never shorter than the spoken line + 0.6 s.
  - After text finishes animating in, hold it for roughly (letters ÷ 15 + 1.5) s in English, (characters ÷ 4.5 + 1.5) s in Chinese; `readcheck.mjs` checks this for you.
  - Hold a title card at least 4 s.
  - Give failures and gags enough time to be understood.
  - Fast is fine; make it fast with fewer words per screen, not by cutting before people finish reading.

## 8. Camera: every shot needs a reason

- Use at least **four different camera moves** and real changes of framing. 2D has a camera too: push, pull, parallax, focus pulls, frames within frames.
- **One signature shot** people remember: a oner, a scale reveal, a transition made from the medium itself.
- **Design transitions inside the medium** (a page turn, a carved line growing, ink spreading), as one consistent grammar. Avoid default fades and hard cuts.
- At key moments the subject fills at least a third of the frame height, with clear staging and a readable silhouette.

## 9. Performance

- **Anticipation, action, follow-through** on every meaningful move. Characters change emotion. They do not just slide across the screen.
- **Motion continuity**, especially for characters built from code rigs:
  - Blend every pose with keyframes and easing; never switch poses inside an `if`. The only exception is a deliberate one-frame comic pop.
  - Check shoulders and arms on a large action test sheet (reach, raise, run, kneel) before shooting (TECHNIQUE.md §10).
  - Held props sit **between the palms**, at a depth between the two arms. A hand-over interpolates from one palm to the other. A rolling object turns by distance ÷ radius.
  - Step through key actions at 0.2 s intervals, enlarged.
- Check every expression at final size, especially eyebrow direction: "worried" and "angry" are one flip apart.

## 10. The failures we saw most

- Subject too small, too far away, or pushed against the frame edge.
- Too dark to read, or a colour laid on the same colour (red on red).
- Subtitles covering the subject.
- A gag or failure too fast to understand.
- Blank frames in transitions.
- A timed effect (iris, zoom, follow cam) that doesn't track the subject after the camera moves (one world → screen function, TECHNIQUE.md §2).

## 11. Before you deliver

- Run the review loop (TECHNIQUE.md §8): contact sheets, 0.2 s strips of key actions, one full-speed viewing with sound.
- **One fix round.** Fix everything the review and the checks below find in one round, then check once more. Small fixes that second check turns up (a level, a frame) belong to the same round; anything bigger, tell the user in one line when you deliver. The user's notes after delivery are new rounds: change only what they ask.
- **Not the demo again.** After the treatment, read `DEMO.md` and compare: structure, opening, signature shot, camera path, score shape, ending. At least four of the six must differ; rethink the ones that match. Before delivery, put your contact sheet next to the demo poster (`styles/<slug>/poster.jpg`) as a last check.
- Voice: every line transcribes back correctly (speech-to-text check). For Chinese, one misheard character in a short line is normal: listen, and if it is right, let the check expect what the model heard (TECHNIQUE.md §4).
- Loudness about −14 LUFS; no black frames, no NaN frames; subtitles in sync and not covering key action.
- Every row of the sound design table is actually in the mix.
- No LemoLab sign-off: `grep -rniE "lemo ?lab|opus 5\.5" <project folder>` finds nothing outside `LICENSE`, `CREDITS` and the library's path in `LIB=` lines, and you have watched the last seconds of the film (text drawn into an image can't be grepped).

**Deliver**, in the project folder (the complete list):

- `<name>.mp4` (24 fps unless `STYLE.md` sets another rate, about −14 LUFS) and `poster.jpg`;
- `<name>.srt`, when the film has narration, dialogue or subtitles;
- `TREATMENT.md`;
- `CREDITS`: every third-party asset in the film (sample libraries, music, fonts, images, the voice engine) with its source and licence (TECHNIQUE.md §11);
- the source, with a one-command `build.sh` (TECHNIQUE.md §2).

**Tell the user**, in their language: where the project folder and the film are; that `CREDITS` lists the third-party assets in the film and their licences; and that they are responsible for the materials they use in it.

## 12. Copyright red lines

- References teach grammar only. Don't copy characters, designs, melodies, shots, logos or type designs.
- No existing works, games, brands or events appear in the film unless the user owns them or has the right to use them. That includes the logos, photos and footage the user hands you: use them when they say they have the right, otherwise draw fictional stand-ins.
- Some of our demos are unofficial fan films of real events or characters. Keep the style, and never carry those names, marks or characters into a user's film.

# Maintaining the library

**For the repository owner only.** If you are making a film for a user, go back to [`AGENTS.md`](AGENTS.md): nothing here applies.

## Add a style

Work in `styles/<slug>/` (lowercase letters, digits, hyphens; unique). Start from the templates in `styles/_template/`.

| File | What it holds |
|---|---|
| `style.json` | the only metadata source: `slug`, `num`, `en`, `cn`, `category_en`, `category_cn`, `film`, `line`, `line_cn`, `uses`, `frame_sec`, `dur` |
| `STYLE.md` | the style's invariants only: look, materials and rendering, colour logic, type, motion, camera grammar, sound palette, the medium's pitfalls, native moves, range of variation. No story, arc, beat table, durations or end card. Ends with a link to `DEMO.md` |
| `DEMO.md` | opens with "One example among many. Don't reuse its story, arc, shots, props or timings." Then the demo's story and structure, shot list, score structure, palette and props, end card (the "LemoLab × Claude Opus 5.5" sign-off lives only here, as the library demo's), build notes and code entry points, and for a scene style the `content.json` fields |
| `demo/` | the source, a one-command `build.sh` and `CREDITS` are committed, for agents to read. `TREATMENT.md`, `PRODUCTION_LOG.md`, fonts, audio, textures and models stay local (gitignored); `CREDITS` names every asset so it can be found again |
| `demo/stills/` | stills the docs link (`styleframe.jpg` is the gallery card) |
| `<slug>.mp4`, `<slug>.srt`, `poster.jpg` | the 1080p film, its subtitles when it is spoken, its poster |

Assets are CC0, CC BY or OFL only, each in `demo/CREDITS`. No watermark on any film. Real people, brands and events appear only in an unofficial fan film; its `DEMO.md` says so.

Rules for library demos only (a user's film follows `DIRECTOR.md`, not these):

- **Bilingual subtitles, one line per language.** Each cue has one Chinese line and one English line, never wrapped. When a line is too long, split it into two cues.
- **Comparisons hold still before the verdict.** When the film compares options (four bridges, three plans), each one is fully in frame and held at least 2.5 s before it is judged, so the viewer can read it.

## Register

1. **Number.** `num` in `style.json` is the next free number after the highest in `styles/*/style.json` (two digits as a string, e.g. `"55"`); it orders the gallery within a category.
2. `python3 styleboard/build.py` reads every `styles/*/style.json` and rewrites the gallery data, the grids and counts in `README.md` (English) and `README.zh-CN.md` (Chinese), `styles/README.md` and the style list in `AGENTS.md`. Never edit those generated parts by hand. The rest of the two READMEs is written by hand: change both together (e.g. the **New** line). Then `python3 styleboard/build.py --frames <slug>` (the README grid frame at `frame_sec`) and `sh styleboard/frames.sh <slug>` (the gallery card from `demo/stills/styleframe.jpg`).
3. `sh tools/web_cuts.sh` makes the 720p web cut in `.release/web/` (only for films that are new or changed).

## Gates

- **Human:** approve the style frame before production, and the finished film.
- **Machine:** `asr_check.py` passes on every line; `mux.sh` reports about −14 LUFS and no warning; `readcheck.mjs` passes; `python3 tools/release.py check --strict <slug>` is clean (it needs the Register steps above). It also stops images under `styles/` that no committed file names (by name or pattern), demo files that nothing reached from the style's entries (STYLE.md, DEMO.md, build.sh, index.html…) loads, and process wording (`PRODUCTION_LOG`, review notes; the list is `PROCESS_WORDS` in the script) in any committed text.
- **Real events and products:** every fact on screen and in the voice-over comes from an official source, kept in `demo/FACTS.md` (claim, URL, quoted wording); check the final script against it before the last render.

## Publish

1. `sh tools/publish.sh` uploads the full films (`films` release) and the 720p web cuts (`web` release, used by the gallery), then verifies them. Per-demo resource packs are no longer published.
2. `git status --short`, `git add -A`, commit.
3. Push `main`, then watch CI (`gh run watch`): the gallery build fails when a card links a film that isn't on the `web` release.

The Pages build (`build.py --site`) also writes the OPUSCAR 98 page (`opuscar98/`, from `styleboard/opuscar98.html`), `llms.txt` and `sitemap.xml`, and puts the canonical link, share-card tags and JSON-LD (upstream repo and author) in each page's head. They pick up the style count by themselves; the film's runtime is `FEATURE['dur']` in `build.py`.

Don't push before the upload has finished, and don't commit `tools/assets.json` from a failed run.

## Revise a style

Back up first (old versions move out of the repository, not into git). Re-render, replace `<slug>.mp4`, and run `sh tools/publish.sh`: it re-uploads the film and refreshes its web cut.

## Directory edition

The Claude plugin directory lists a self-contained build of the plugin, on the orphan branch `directory` (the submission tracks that branch; `main` stays what visitors see). It carries the guides, every `STYLE.md` / `style.json` / `DEMO.md`, `core/` (without the Poly Haven models, which only demo code uses) and its own `README.md`, `SECURITY.md` and `SKILL.md`: nothing is cloned or fetched to tell the agent what to do, there are no demo sources, and Chinese edge-tts narration is used only with the user's consent. The sources of the plugin-only files are in `tools/directory/`; the build and its checks (file sizes, personal info) are in `tools/directory.py`.

After a release on `main` (new styles, changed guides or tools):

1. `git worktree add ../lemo-opuscar-directory directory` (once; reuse it afterwards).
2. `python3 tools/directory.py <version> --into ../lemo-opuscar-directory`, with a version above the branch's current `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` (new styles or features: 1.1.0; fixes only: 1.0.1). The directory treats each version number as a release, so the script refuses the same or a lower one; `--same-version` is only for fixing a version that was never published. It also stops when a guide changed so much that one of its edits no longer applies: update `EDITS` in the script.
3. `claude plugin validate ../lemo-opuscar-directory`, then commit there (`Lemo-Opuscar <version>, plugin directory edition`) and push `directory`. The directory scans each push and publishes the new version.

# Make a style your own

A user makes a style of their own, in one of two ways: **change a library style**, or **start from a blank page**. You plan it with them, one question at a time or in free conversation, prove the look with a style frame and make a short demo film. When they confirm it, you keep it in their own folder in the same shape as a library style. From then on they name it like any library style when they ask for a film. It lives outside the library and never changes it.

Use this guide when the user wants to change a style or make their own ("I want to change this style", "make my own version", "start from scratch", "我想改风格", "做成我自己的风格", "从空白开始"), or when they name a style that is in their own folder. Everything else in a film follows [`AGENTS.md`](AGENTS.md) as usual, with the exceptions this guide gives.

Talk to the user in their language. Write the files in English, like the library, with the style's name in both languages.

## Where it lives

Until the user confirms it (§6), a style is a draft in the demo film's project folder. Confirmed styles live in **`~/lemo-my-styles/`**, outside the library, so library updates and uninstalling never touch them. `~/lemo-my-styles/README.md` lists every style, one row each (English and Chinese name, slug, base, one line on what it is, and the folder when it isn't in `~/lemo-my-styles/`): it's how a later session finds a style by name. If the user wants a style kept in another folder, keep it there and still add its row, with the full path, to `~/lemo-my-styles/README.md`.

Each style has its own folder, `~/lemo-my-styles/<slug>/`, shaped like a library style (`MAINTAINING.md` **Add a style**, without the gallery and the release):

| File | What it holds |
|---|---|
| `style.json` | `slug`, `en`, `cn`, `based_on` (the base slug; from a blank page, the technique base), `borrows` (slugs moves were taken from, may be empty), `size` (only when the default isn't 1920×1080, e.g. `"1080x1440"`), `library_version` (`git -C "$LIB" rev-parse --short HEAD`, or the plugin version when `$LIB` isn't a git clone), `created`, `line`, `line_cn` |
| `STYLE.md` | the style's invariants only, in the sections of a library `STYLE.md` (11 in most; a changed style keeps its base's): no story, beat table, durations or end card |
| `CHANGES.md` | one row per decision: section, base, now, why. From a blank page, "base" is the technique base's value, or "—" for something new. This is what the user approves and what you check the demo film against |
| `DEMO.md` | how the demo film was made, like a library `DEMO.md`: it opens with "One example among many. Don't reuse its story, arc, shots, props or timings.", then the story, shots, palette, score, build notes and which file draws what. It stands in for the film's `TREATMENT.md`, which isn't kept |
| `demo/` | the demo film's source with a one-command `build.sh` and `CREDITS`: the code and the small assets it needs to rebuild (fonts, data), not renders, frames, `node_modules`, virtual environments or caches |
| `styleframe.jpg` | the approved style frame |
| `styleframe-vs-base.jpg` | changing a library style only: the same frame, base on the left, theirs on the right |
| `test.mp4`, `test.jpg` | the demo film and its poster |

Never write into `styles/` or edit the library's guides for this. The name and slug must not match a library style or a row in `~/lemo-my-styles/README.md`.

## 1. Where to start

- **Change a library style.** The user names one (see **Finding the style** in `AGENTS.md`). If they haven't, do as **Finding the style** does for a film: the full list of library styles in your message, the gallery link, two or three suggestions on top when you know what they'll use it for, then a plain-text question asking them to type the name (not `AskUserQuestion`). One base only. If they want to mix two, take the one whose §1 *Essence* is closest as the base and take only what they want from the other, as changes (list it in `borrows`).
- **Start from a blank page.** The user describes the look in their own words, or brings a picture or a film they like. Choose one library style as the **technique base** (the closest materials and engine: what the code will build on) and at most two to borrow moves from. Make that the first question: your choice and why in one line each, with the next closest as the other options.

Either way, read the base `STYLE.md` in full before the first question. In this flow you may read the base's `DEMO.md` (and, in skill mode, get its source with `setup.sh demo <slug>`) before any treatment: the style frame needs its techniques. The demo film's story must still differ from the base demo's (DIRECTOR.md §11, *Not the demo again*, compared with the base).

## 2. Plan it together

Interview the user until every section of their `STYLE.md` is decided and they know what each choice costs.

**How to ask**

- **One question per message.** Use the `AskUserQuestion` tool: 2–3 options, the one you recommend first and marked (Recommended), each with one line on what it does to the film, and **Free conversation** (in their language) as the last option. Without the tool, a short numbered list with your recommendation, and free conversation as its last line.
- **Free conversation.** When they pick it, stop asking one by one. Post in the chat a checklist: what's decided, and each open item with your recommendation (when changing a library style, also its group from the table below). They answer in their own words, in any order, several at once, or ask you back. When they aren't sure about an item, give two or three concrete directions for it. Update the checklist each round; when everything is decided, or they say "you decide", go to the summary.
- Every question has your recommendation and the reason, drawn from the base `STYLE.md` and what the user said, with concrete examples from this style, not generic words.
- Don't ask what you can look up (the base `STYLE.md`, the library, their files).
- **About ten questions at most**, the technique base included. When more sections are in play, ask related ones together (motion with sound, camera with native moves). If they say "you decide" ("你定", "都按推荐"), take your recommendations for the rest, list them in one message and go on.

**The order** (skip what they've already said):

1. **Use.** What films they'll make with it, for whom, where they'll post them, and so the frame size (a vertical feed needs 1080×1920 or 1080×1440). Their brand or IP: colours, logo, font, a character. They give you the files later.
2. **What changes.**
   - *Change a library style*: first show the three groups as a short message, using this style's own sections and examples. Then ask which parts they want to touch (several may be picked).

     Section numbers below are the usual ones; some styles (Edit & Documentary above all) number or split them differently, so go by the section's subject in the base `STYLE.md`.

     | Group | Sections of `STYLE.md` | What to tell the user |
     |---|---|---|
     | **Safe to change** | §3 colour (the palette within its logic), §4 type, §5 motion (tempo, how much moves), §7 sound palette (instruments, density), §8 native moves (add or swap one) | the style stays itself; give 2–3 ideas for each |
     | **Changes its character** | §2 materials and rendering, the colour logic itself in §3, §6 camera grammar | possible; say what the style loses with each change |
     | **Can't change** | §1 essence (and its "what it is not"), §10 engine | that's a different style, not a version of this one. Say so and suggest a closer base |

     When a safe change narrows a phrase in §1 (three inks become two), adjust that phrase; the essence stays.
   - *From a blank page*: the essence first, one sentence on what it is and one on what it is not. Then the materials.
3. **Section by section**, only the sections in play, in `STYLE.md` order: materials and rendering, colour, type, motion, camera, sound, native moves. Give 2–3 concrete directions for each.
4. **The name**: English, Chinese or both, and the slug.

**Help them change it well.** Most users know the feeling they want, not the section. While you ask:

- Start from the use. The changes follow what the films are for: a weekly brand bulletin needs readable type and a fixed opening, a kids' channel needs bigger shapes and slower reading.
- Turn vague wishes into options, never silent edits:

  | They say | Usually means |
  |---|---|
  | more premium, 高级 | fewer colours, stronger contrast between light and dark, slower motion, more empty space, lighter type |
  | younger, livelier, 活泼 | a brighter accent, cuts on the beat, bouncier easing, more percussion |
  | calmer, 安静 | slower tempo, longer holds, fewer moving things, sparser instruments |
  | like our brand, 像我们品牌 | the brand colour as the accent, not the ground; the brand font for titles; the logo at the open and the end |

- **Brand.** Keep the base's light-and-dark structure so text stays readable, and bring the brand colour in as the accent first. A brand font must cover the film's language (Chinese glyphs for a Chinese film) and allow use in video. Logos and fonts come from the user.
- **A reference.** Name two or three things in it that make it work, map each to a section, and say which ones would touch §1 essence.
- **Keep the signature.** The native move is what makes the style recognisable: swap at most one.
- **Changes that travel together.** Faster motion needs denser sound. A darker palette needs the type contrast checked. A new material brings its own pitfalls into §9.
- **Up to five changes** per round when changing a library style; more are hard to judge. A change the film's language forces (a Chinese font when the base has none) doesn't count.
- **Code draws everything**, as in the library: no image or video generation, which the user may not have. Anything that isn't code (pictures, fonts, stroke or map data, samples) is the user's own or openly licensed, as in TECHNIQUE.md §11, and named in `CREDITS`. A licence the user has to agree to is asked once, and their answer goes into `STYLE.md` so later films don't ask again. If something can't work, say so and offer the closest change code can draw.
- **What doesn't need a style.** Story, structure, opening, ending, cast, sets, pacing and voice (§11 *Variation space*) are free in every film. If that's all they want, they don't need their own style: they say it when they ask for a film.

When the plan is complete, show the user a short summary in their language: each decision, before and after, and what it costs. **Wait for their OK**, then write it down.

## 3. Write it down

Make the demo film's project folder now (`films/<slug>-test/` in a clone, `<slug>-test/` in the user's folder in skill mode) and work only there until §6. The draft style goes in its `style/` folder, with the files of the table above.

- **`STYLE.md`**:
  - *Change a library style*: a full copy of the base `STYLE.md` with the changes written into their sections, so it reads like any style prompt (no "see the base" gaps). Change the title to the new name and add one line under it: `Based on <base name> (<base slug>) from Lemo-Opuscar.`
  - *From a blank page*: all 11 sections written from the plan, with §10 engine from the technique base for now (§5 points it at the style's own code). Under the title: `Made from a blank page; techniques from <base name> (<base slug>) in Lemo-Opuscar.`
  - When the default size isn't 1920×1080, one more line under the title: `Default size: 1080×1440.`
  - Links: the style's own `DEMO.md` and `demo/` (they exist after §5) stay relative; links to the base become `$LIB/styles/<base slug>/…`. Keep every pitfall in §9 that still applies, and add the ones the changes bring.
- **`CHANGES.md`** and **`style.json`** as in the table above.

## 4. Prove the look

Render one style frame with the real drawing code, starting from the base style's techniques (copy code into the project, never edit the library). Check it against the new `STYLE.md` and fix what's off, once.

- *Change a library style*: render the same frame a second time with the base's settings (its colours, materials and type; a stand-in font when the base's has no glyphs for the film's language), and put the two side by side, base on the left, so only the changes differ: `style/styleframe-vs-base.jpg` (`core/render/sheet.py` tiles stills).
- *From a blank page*: there's nothing to compare against. Show the frame on its own, next to the user's reference if they gave one.

Save the frame as `style/styleframe.jpg`. **Show it to the user and wait.** If they want more, update `STYLE.md` and `CHANGES.md` and render again. If it still isn't right after two rounds of their notes, say so and suggest a closer base.

## 5. The demo film (15–30 s)

A short film whose job is to show the style working, not a full production:

- **Topic**: the user's own if they give one; otherwise a simple one with movement and a little light (a kite on a windy beach, the first tram of the morning). Not the base demo's story.
- **Every row of `CHANGES.md` is clearly on screen** at least once, and the native move appears once.
- Music and sound effects, no voice and no subtitles unless the user asks (a voice is a separate test).
- Treatment: one structure is enough (no three candidates). No storyboard. DIRECTOR.md's counts are written for longer films: at this length one real silence and three kinds of camera move are enough.
- **Checks**, as for any film: DIRECTOR.md §11, with its one fix round (no LemoLab sign-off in the film).

Then save it into `style/`:

- the film and its poster as `test.mp4` and `test.jpg`;
- the source as `demo/`, with `CREDITS` and a `build.sh` that runs from there: `LIB=<path>` at the top, library files as `$LIB/…` (never `../..`, also in code copied from the base), and everything it writes going to `${OUT:-<a folder outside demo/>}`. Run it once from the saved folder with `OUT` set to a temporary folder, and check that `demo/` holds the same files afterwards. Code copied from the library keeps its MIT notice in `demo/CREDITS`; that is a licence, not a credit in the film;
- `DEMO.md`;
- From a blank page, point §10 *Engine* in `STYLE.md` at the files in `demo/` that draw the style, then at the technique base.

## 6. Keep it

Show the user the demo film: where it is, and each change with the second where it can be seen. Then ask with `AskUserQuestion`:

1. **Keep it as my style** (Recommended): check that the name and slug are still free, copy `style/` to `~/lemo-my-styles/<slug>/` (or the folder they want), add its row to `~/lemo-my-styles/README.md` (create it if it's missing: a title and a table with one row per style), and tell them where it is and how to use it ("Make a film in my <name> style about…").
2. **One more round**: change what they ask (§7), then ask again.
3. **Not now**: leave it in the project folder. Tell them its path, and that saying "keep the style in <path> as my style" later saves it then.

Only a kept style is theirs: listed when the skill starts, and found by name.

## 7. Revise or use it

- **Not right yet**: change `STYLE.md` and `CHANGES.md`, then render the style frame and the demo film again and replace `demo/` and `DEMO.md`. Change only what the user asks.
- **Using it**: find it through `~/lemo-my-styles/README.md`. Read its `STYLE.md` in place of a library `STYLE.md` and follow the normal workflow in `AGENTS.md`, treatment first, at the style's default size unless the user asks for another. For techniques, read the style's own `DEMO.md` and `demo/` first, then the base's (`$LIB/styles/<based_on>/DEMO.md`). The demo film is one example: never reuse its story, shots or timeline. The films are the user's: no LemoLab credit, no watermark.
- **After a library update**: if the base `STYLE.md` changed since `library_version`, mention it once and offer to bring the useful fixes into their copy. Don't change their style without asking.

## 👋 关于我 我是 **Lemomo**，更多信息见我的 [GitHub 主页](https://github.com/lemomo-ai)。 > **这不是一个 awesome 合集。** 这里所有的片子都是我自己用 Claude Opus 5.5 做的。
> 风格是按 Opus 5.5 调出来的，换成其他模型不保证能做出同样的效果。 ![全部风格](docs/cover.jpg) 每一支片子都是 AI agent 写代码导演、作画、配乐、混音的： - 🎨 **画面**：Canvas 和 WebGL 页面逐帧渲染 - 🎵 **音乐**：用免费采样库写的原创配乐 - 🎙️ **配音**：TTS 语音合成 不用视频生成，也不用素材库画面。 ## 怎么用 两种用法，推荐装 skill，最省事。 ### 方式一：装成 skill（推荐） 在终端里： ```sh claude plugin marketplace add lemomo-ai/lemo-opuscar claude plugin install lemo-opuscar@lemolab ``` 之后在任何目录都能用。 - 第一次使用时，它会把指南、工具和风格提示词下载到 `~/lemo-opuscar`，所有片子共用这一份。 - 每支片子的工程，从源码到成片，都放在你发起时所在的文件夹里。 - 其他 agent 可以把 [`plugin/skills/lemo-opuscar/`](plugin/skills/lemo-opuscar/) 复制到它们的 skills 目录。 ### 方式二：clone 仓库 ```sh git clone https://github.com/lemomo-ai/lemo-opuscar.git cd lemo-opuscar claude ``` 片子做到仓库里的 `films/<名字>/`。 ### 然后直接说 > 用**油画厚涂**风格做一支 30 秒的片子，讲我家那只每天在窗台等我下班的橘猫。 > 用**点云测绘**风格做一支 40 秒的片子，讲我们镇后山那座废弃的采石场，数据用公开的激光扫描。 风格用中文名、英文名或文件夹名都行，全部风格见[风格索引](styles/README.md)。 还没想好也没关系：装成 skill 的，输入 `/lemo-opuscar:lemo-opuscar` 直接启动。它先问你用什么语言，再问这次想做什么：用库里的风格做片、[把风格改成你自己的](#改成你自己的风格)，或者用你存过的风格。 它开工前只问你一次： - 主题里它定不了的事； - 你有没有自己的**配音、音乐或其他素材**； - 要不要先看**分镜故事板**。要看的话，它会停一次，给你看用真实风格画出来的关键镜头；不看就直接做完成片。 agent 会读三份指南，像一个小工作室一样开工。
指南是英文写给 agent 看的，你用中文跟它说就行，片子的配音和字幕默认跟你用的语言一致。 | 文件 | 给 agent 的东西 | |---|---| | [`DIRECTOR.md`](DIRECTOR.md) | 怎么导：故事、声音、节奏、镜头、表演、自检 | | [`TECHNIQUE.md`](TECHNIQUE.md) | 怎么做：逐帧渲染、配音、配乐、混音 | | `styles/<风格>/STYLE.md` | 这个风格长什么样、听起来什么样；故事由你定 | ### 改成你自己的风格 每个人想要的都不一样：有自己的品牌色、logo、IP 和账号调性。现在你可以把库里的风格改成只属于你的，或者从空白做一个库里没有的。走的就是我自己往库里加新风格的流程。

库里的风格 · 瑞士动态排版
平面网格、一个信号色、动作卡着节拍。
我的风格 · 材质网格 · ▶ 31 秒 demo 片
留下瑞士排版的网格、节拍和字体，换成陶土、塑料、绒布、玻璃和铬的实物：俯视是一张海报，镜头一倾全是实物。
**两个入口。** 启动 skill 后在入口里选，或者一句话直接说： > 我想把**浮世绘**风格改成我自己的版本。 > 从空白开始，做一个黑板粉笔画的风格，暖一点、慢一点。 - **改库里的风格**：它列出全部风格和画廊链接，你打字说改哪一个。 - **从空白开始**：用你自己的话描述想要的样子，也可以给一张喜欢的图或一支片。Claude 从库里挑一个最接近的风格当技法底子，说清楚为什么选它，你点头或者换一个。 **接下来五步：** 1. **一个问题一个问题定方案。** 每个问题都带几个选项，推荐的排第一，附上理由。大概会问： - 拿来做什么：做什么片、发在哪个平台（竖屏就用 1080×1920 或 1080×1440），有没有品牌色、logo、字体或固定角色； - 想改哪里：改库里风格时，它先把风格分成三组讲给你听，**放心改**（配色、字体、动作快慢、声音、标志镜头）、**一改就变味**（材质和画法、配色的逻辑、镜头语法）、**不能改**（风格的本质，改了就是另一个风格）； - 每一项往哪个方向改，最后起名字。 说得模糊也行，比如「高级一点」「活泼一点」，它会翻译成具体的改法让你挑。嫌慢就选每题最后的「自由对话」，直接聊；随时说「你定」，剩下的它按推荐填好。改库里风格时一轮最多改五处；全部用代码画，不用生图。 2. **看汇总，点头。** 每一项改前是什么、改后是什么、代价是什么，你点头了它才写下来。 3. **先看一张风格图。** 用真实的绘制代码画出来。改库里风格的，同一个画面用原风格再出一张，左边原版、右边你的并排放。不满意就说，两轮还不对它会直说，建议换一个更接近的底子。 4. **一支 15–30 秒的 demo 片。** 每一处改动都在画面里出现，配音乐和音效。它自己检查、修一轮再交给你。 5. **满意了再固化。** 它问你：固化、再改一轮，还是先不固化。你点头之前，一切都只在这次的项目文件夹里。 固化以后，风格存在 `~/lemo-my-styles/<名字>/`，和库里的风格同一个结构：风格说明、改了什么、demo 片和它的源码，以后做片能接着用这些技法。之后像用库里的风格一样叫它的名字：“用我的**夜浮世绘**风格做一支 30 秒的片子，讲……”。挑风格时，你自己的风格排在最前面。 库更新、重装 skill 都不会动它们。底子风格以后更新了，它会提一句，问你要不要把有用的修复同步过来。Claude 照着 [`MY-STYLES.md`](MY-STYLES.md) 一步步做。 ### 开始之前 - 一支片子 agent 大约要做 30–60 分钟，token 用量不小。 - 需要 Node 20+、ffmpeg 7+ 和 Python 3.11+（或 [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/)），其余由 agent 安装。Ubuntu 24.04 自带的 ffmpeg 是 6.1，版本太旧，请换成[静态版](https://johnvansickle.com/ffmpeg/)。 - 默认输出 1920×1080、24 fps，其他尺寸可以指定。 ### 更新和卸载 更新，然后重启 Claude Code（`~/lemo-opuscar` 里的库会在下一次做片时自动更新）： ```sh claude plugin marketplace update lemolab && claude plugin update lemo-opuscar@lemolab ``` 更新后照常说要做什么片；想把风格改成自己的，看[上面](#改成你自己的风格)。 卸载，然后删除 `~/lemo-opuscar`： ```sh claude plugin uninstall lemo-opuscar@lemolab ``` 你自己的风格存在 `~/lemo-my-styles/`，更新和卸载都不会删；不要了就自己删掉这个文件夹。 一直卡住就[提个 issue](https://github.com/lemomo-ai/lemo-opuscar/issues)。 ## 风格 点图片看它的 `STYLE.md`。 ### 🆕 最新 · 2026-10-29

# Technique: how the films are built

Every film here is made from code: no video generation, no stock footage. This page explains the pipeline, to reproduce with our tools in `core/` or in your own stack. Pair it with [`DIRECTOR.md`](DIRECTOR.md) and one `styles/<slug>/STYLE.md`. Every command and flag is in [`core/README.md`](core/README.md).

```
timeline (single source of truth)
   ├─► picture:  web page with render(t) ──► headless Chrome, frame by frame ──► video.mp4
   ├─► voice:    TTS per line ──► speech-to-text check ──► word timings
   ├─► music:    score from the same timeline (samples + synthesis) ──► stems
   ├─► sound:    procedural foley at event times
   └─► subtitles: .srt + burned-in captions
mix (duck, compress, balance) ──► mux with ffmpeg, two-pass loudnorm −14 LUFS ──► film.mp4
```

## 1. Requirements and install

System tools, which the user installs: **Node 20+**, **ffmpeg 7+** (6.x under-reports audio length through `loudnorm`, and `mux.sh` then rejects the file as cut off), and **Python 3.11+** or [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/). Developed on macOS (Apple silicon); Linux should work; on Windows use WSL. 3D and shader-heavy styles want a GPU.

Everything else installs in tiers, from the library root (`$LIB` in skill mode). Install a tier only when the film needs it:

| Command | Adds | Size |
|---|---|---|
| `sh plugin/skills/lemo-opuscar/scripts/setup.sh deps` | core: npm packages, headless browser, Python `.venv` (numpy, scipy, soundfile, soxr, pillow): render, synthesize sound, mux | ~350 MB |
| `… setup.sh deps voice` | Kokoro + model (English, offline), edge-tts (Chinese, online), faster-whisper (voice check) | ~0.55 GB + a Whisper model on first check (~145 MB for English, ~480 MB for Chinese) |
| `… setup.sh deps music` | numba, for plucked strings (`pluck.py`); the sampler itself needs only the core | ~140 MB |
| `sh tools/fetch.sh instruments <lib>` | a sample library: `freepats`, `karoryfer`, `salamander`, `vcsl`, `vsco2ce` or `all` | 70–400 MB each |
| `sh tools/fetch.sh hdri` | HDRIs for 3D styles | 12 MB |

Some styles need packages of their own (a LiDAR reader, a slide-scan decoder, a CAD importer); the style's `STYLE.md` lists them. They are packages, not system tools: install them yourself into a private venv or `node_modules` in the project folder, never into `$LIB/.venv`.

A synthesized score needs no big download; `sampler.py` names the library to fetch when an instrument is missing. A pack needs about twice its size free while it unpacks. Downloads come from npm, PyPI, GitHub Releases and Hugging Face (`HF_ENDPOINT` sets a mirror).

## 2. The picture is a function of time

Each film is a folder with an `index.html` (`<demo>` in the commands) that exposes:

```js
window.DUR = 54.2;                 // seconds
window.render = (t) => { ... };    // draw the frame at time t, deterministic
window.READY = true;               // set once fonts and images are loaded
window.EV = [{t, type, ...}];      // optional: sound / cue events for the mixer
window.TEXTS = (t) => [{id, text, x0, y0, x1, y1}];   // optional: every text visible at t, for readcheck
```

**Paths:** pages reach library files with absolute URLs (`/core/lib.js`, `/node_modules/three/build/three.module.js`); scripts and `build.sh` use `$LIB`. Never `../..`.

A `build.sh` that works in both modes (in skill mode, put `LIB=<path setup.sh printed>` at the top):

```sh
#!/bin/sh
set -e
HERE=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)
LIB=${LIB:-$(cd "$HERE/../.." && pwd)}          # clone mode: <repo>/films/<name>/
export LIB
[ -f "$LIB/core/render/video.mjs" ] || { echo "set LIB to the library folder"; exit 1; }
cd "$LIB"
node core/render/events.mjs "$HERE"
node core/render/video.mjs "$HERE" --fps 24 --out "$HERE/out/video.mp4"
"$LIB/.venv/bin/python" "$HERE/mix.py"                               # score, foley, voice → out/mix.wav
sh core/render/mux.sh "$HERE/out/video.mp4" "$HERE/out/mix.wav" "$HERE/<name>.mp4" 24
```

Rules that keep it reliable:

- **Deterministic.** No `Date.now()`, no `Math.random()` without a seed (`core/lib.js` has `mulberry` and `hash`), no state carried from the previous frame. Any frame can be rendered alone, in any order, by any worker.
- **Canvas 2D** for most 2D styles; **three.js** for 3D (§9); **WebGL2** shaders for post passes (film damage, CRT, ink redraw).
- **Animate on twos where the style wants it** (12 fps stepping for stop-motion, pixel or cel looks), but keep the camera and light smooth every frame. A stepped camera reads as lag.
- **One world → screen function.** Any effect that follows a subject (iris, zoom, spotlight) goes through it. Never hand-type screen coordinates.
- **Draw for the frame you render.** The default is 1920×1080; for another size pass `--size WxH` (e.g. `1080x1920`) to every render tool and lay the page out from `innerWidth` × `innerHeight`.

Capture (`core/render/`):

```sh
node core/render/still.mjs <demo> 1.5 12 --range 0:50:2   # review stills; exits on page errors
node core/render/video.mjs <demo> --fps 24 --workers 3     # all frames → <demo>/out/video.mp4
node core/render/events.mjs <demo>                         # export DUR + EV → events.json
node core/render/readcheck.mjs <demo>                      # every on-screen text stays long enough to read
```

To render a second version with other content, pass it to the page and give it its own output: `--q 'content=content_alt.json' --out …/alt.mp4` (the same for `events.mjs`).

Capture is fast because of **JPEG screenshots**, **one browser per worker** and **grain added in ffmpeg**: grain drawn in the page makes every frame incompressible and slow.

## 3. One timeline drives everything

Keep sections, tempo, beats and hit points in one file (`timeline.js`). Export it to JSON and let the score, the mixer, the subtitles and the checks read the same numbers:

```js
export const SECS = [{ id: 'chase', t: 12.0, bpm: 144, beats: 12 }, ...];
export const HIT  = { pratfall: ['chase', 6], ... };   // section + beat
```

A small script (`cuecheck.py`, in `styles/<slug>/demo/tools/` of several demos) compares every visual hit with the music cue it should land on. Aim for 0 ms.

## 4. Voice

- **TTS is only the default.** If the user brings a recording or names a voice, use that. Otherwise:
  - **English**: [Kokoro](https://github.com/thewh1teagle/kokoro-onnx), local, many voices (an unknown `voice` name makes `tts.py` print the full list; `af_` / `am_` are American, `bf_` / `bm_` British; cast the narrator for this film, not the demo's). `core/tts/tts.py lines.json out/` writes one WAV per line and a durations file. Its Chinese voices (`"lang": "cmn"`) work offline but sound plain.
  - **Chinese**: `core/tts/tts_zh.py lines.json out/` uses [edge-tts](https://github.com/rany2/edge-tts) with Microsoft's neural voices (`zh-CN-XiaoxiaoNeural`, `zh-CN-YunxiNeural`…), with the same outputs as `tts.py`, a rate per line and the silence trimmed. **It needs a network connection.**
- Spell numbers out in the TTS text and write them as digits in the subtitles.
- **Check every line**: `core/tts/asr_check.py` transcribes each WAV with faster-whisper and compares it with the script (`--lang zh`: numbers by value, so 十九 matches 19, and the rest character by character); re-generate until it exits 0. A misheard character in a short Chinese line is normal: listen, and if it is right, put what the model heard in the line's `asr` field. It also writes word timestamps for placing lines and subtitles.
- **Before mixing**: TTS has a high peak-to-average ratio. Compress the voice first, then balance by RMS: voice about 10 dB above the music.

## 5. Music

Write an original score from the cue map, in the instruments of the style's sound palette; no generic piano and strings.

- **Samples**: `core/audio/sampler.py` plays real instruments from free libraries (VSCO 2 CE, VCSL, FreePats, Karoryfer, Salamander Grand Piano; list and licences in `core/audio/INSTRUMENTS.md`). Write the score as events `(time, instrument, pitch, duration, velocity, pan)`. Long notes are extended seamlessly, and round-robins avoid the machine-gun effect.
- **Plucked and folk strings** (guqin, pipa, shamisen, banjo…): `core/audio/pluck.py`, physical modelling (Karplus–Strong) with bends and vibrato.
- **Synthesis** with numpy for chip tunes, drones and effects; no download needed.
- **Balance the low end.** Synthetic scores get bass-heavy quickly. Measure energy per band after mixing; keep 20–120 Hz around −3 dB relative to the rest, skip pad notes below MIDI 48, and give the bass some 2nd and 3rd harmonics so it speaks on small speakers.

## 6. Sound effects and mix

- `core/audio/sfx.py` synthesises foley procedurally (click, whoosh, thump, ding, paper, noise beds…) with filters, envelopes and `add(buffer, sound, at, gain, pan)`. Drive it from `window.EV`, so every sound sits exactly on its frame.
- **Master**: `sh core/render/mux.sh video.mp4 mix.wav out.mp4 24 [grain]` muxes, runs a two-pass loudnorm to −14 LUFS with a true-peak limit, adds grain in ffmpeg and prints the measured loudness; it exits non-zero on any failure. On light backgrounds use less grain; for pixel and vector styles, none.
- Films with grain baked into the picture compress badly; re-encode with `-tune grain` and a higher CRF.

## 7. Subtitles

- Export `.srt` with `core/render/srt.py cues.json out.srt` (cues = `[{t0, t1, text}]`), and burn styled captions into the page itself: the caption design is part of the style.
- Timing rules are in DIRECTOR.md §7.

## 8. Review loop

1. Contact sheets: a frame every 1–2 s with `still.mjs --range`, tiled with `core/render/sheet.py`. At least two full passes.
2. Frame strips at 0.2 s for every key action: hand-overs, falls, hits.
3. On the final file: `ffmpeg -af ebur128` (loudness), `blackdetect` (blank frames), whisper again on the final mix if it has voice.
4. Watch it once, at full speed, with sound.

## 9. 3D notes

- three.js r170 rendered headless through WebGL2 on the GPU; physical depth of field and GTAO from `core/three/post.js`, rendered at 2× and downsampled.
- Lighting: soft area lights plus a Poly Haven HDRI at low intensity reads more "real" than bright ambient light.
- `core/three/post.js` is written for a perspective camera. For an orthographic camera swap `perspectiveDepthToViewZ` for `orthographicDepthToViewZ` in its depth pass, or the depth of field silently breaks.

## 10. Characters drawn in code

- A 2.5D rig (torso, head, limbs solved per frame) is enough for pantomime.
- Order the shoulder rotation as abduction, then flexion; the reverse order crosses raised arms into an X.
- Let the shoulder girdle rise and move forward as the arm lifts, and don't outline the part of the arm that overlaps the torso: that line is what makes a joint look like a puppet seam.

## 11. Assets, credits and fonts

Only CC0, CC BY or OFL material, each listed in the film's `CREDITS` with its source and licence; `core/audio/sampler.py credits(names)` writes the lines for the instruments you used. Public-domain works count as CC0; "no known restrictions" does not. Data or images under other open licences (ODbL, CC BY-SA, open-hardware licences) only after you have named the licence and its terms (attribution, share-alike) to the user and they agree. The user's own material is fine as it is.

A film that states facts (the Evidence Films styles) keeps a `FACTS.md` in the project folder: each claim with its source URL and the quoted wording, or the measurement that produced it.

Fonts: Google Fonts (OFL), self-hosted in the project. The typefaces a `STYLE.md` names are not in the library; download them (`https://github.com/google/fonts/tree/main/ofl/<family>`) into the project's `fonts/`. `core/fonts/` holds a few Latin display fonts and a Chinese display font with only about 200 glyphs, not enough for running Chinese text. For Chinese, subset a CJK font to the characters you use: the Google Fonts CSS API with `&text=` returns just those glyphs (`https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Noto+Sans+SC:wght@700&text=<URL-encoded characters>`). Download the font file it points to into the project's `fonts/` and load it with `@font-face`; don't link Google Fonts at render time.

## 12. Where to look in our demos

| If you need… | Look at |
|---|---|
| 2D character animation and lip sync | `styles/scifi-toon/`, `styles/cel-anime-80s/` |
| a timeline-driven score with cue checking | `styles/microgame/`, `styles/silent-film/` |
| an image-to-ink redraw and film-damage post pass | `styles/silent-film/demo/engine/` |
| a brush or stroke engine | `styles/watercolor/`, `styles/ink-wash/`, `styles/impasto/` |
| 3D with depth of field and real materials | `styles/brick-toy/`, `styles/paper-popup/` |
| a CRT or VHS look | `core/post/crt.js`, `styles/ascii-crt/`, `styles/backrooms/` |

Each style's `DEMO.md` says how its demo was built. Open it and the code only after your treatment exists, to learn a technique, never to rebuild our film (an Edit & Documentary style's material tools in `demo/tools/` come first: AGENTS.md, "Treatment first"). In skill mode, get the source with `sh <skill folder>/scripts/setup.sh demo <slug>`. Copied demo code often reaches the library with `../..`: replace that with `$LIB` or absolute URLs.

# core/: the shared production tools

Command reference for `core/` and `tools/`. How the pieces fit together is in [`TECHNIQUE.md`](../TECHNIQUE.md). Run commands from the library root (`$LIB` in skill mode); Python is the library's `.venv/bin/python`. `<demo>` is any folder with an `index.html`.

## Install

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `sh plugin/skills/lemo-opuscar/scripts/setup.sh` | find, clone or update the library; prints `LIB=<path>` |
| `… setup.sh deps` | core tier: npm packages, headless browser, `.venv` from `requirements.txt` |
| `… setup.sh deps voice` | adds `requirements-voice.txt` (kokoro-onnx, edge-tts, faster-whisper) and the Kokoro model |
| `… setup.sh deps music` | adds `requirements-music.txt` (numba, for `pluck.py`; `sampler.py` needs only the core) |
| `… setup.sh demo <slug>` | adds one style's demo source and poster (to read, not to render) |
| `sh tools/fetch.sh voice` \| `hdri` \| `instruments <lib>` \| `instruments all` | Kokoro model · HDRIs · a sample library (`freepats`, `karoryfer`, `salamander`, `vcsl`, `vsco2ce`) |

Sizes are in TECHNIQUE.md §1.

## The page contract

| Global | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `window.READY = true` | yes | set once fonts and images are loaded |
| `window.render(t)` | yes | draw the frame at second `t`; deterministic |
| `window.DUR` | video, events, readcheck | film length in seconds |
| `window.EV = [{t, type, …}]` | no | sound and cue events, exported by `events.mjs` |
| `window.TEXTS(t)` | readcheck | `[{id, text, x0, y0, x1, y1}]`: every on-screen text visible at `t`, with its box in pixels. Report an element's **full** text from its first visible frame (a typewriter that reports only the typed letters fails the check) |

The viewport is 1920×1080 at device scale 1, or `--size WxH`. `--q 'k=v&…'` reaches the page as `location.search`. A page error, or an HTTP error on a script, module or the page, stops the tool (exit 1). Other missing files (fetch, images, fonts) print `optional file missing: <URL>` and the tool carries on. The tools wait up to 180 s for `window.READY`.

## Render

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `node core/render/still.mjs <demo> <t> [<t> …] [--range a:b:step] [--prefix t_] [--out dir]` | review stills as JPEGs (default `<demo>/stills/t_<t>.jpg`) |
| `node core/render/video.mjs <demo> [--fps 24] [--workers 3] [--out <demo>/out/video.mp4]` | every frame to a video; up to 6 workers for a single render. Each parallel version needs its own `--out` |
| `node core/render/events.mjs <demo> [--out <file>]` | export `{dur, ev}` to `<demo>/events.json` |

All four page tools take `--size WxH` (default `1920x1080`, even numbers) and `--q 'k=v'`.

**readcheck** asks the page for `window.TEXTS(t)` at every step. Each text must stay fully in frame, unchanged, for at least CJK characters ÷ 4.5 + other non-space characters ÷ 15 + 1.5 s, and never less than `--min`. A new `text` under the same `id` starts a new piece. Subtitles are checked by their `.srt`, not here.

**mux** runs a two-pass `loudnorm` to −14 LUFS / true peak −1.2 dB, adds film grain (`grain` 0 = none) and prints the measured loudness. Silent audio is left at its level with a warning; short audio is padded, long audio cut at the picture's end; missing, damaged or truncated audio is refused. It never leaves a partial file.
